node: Midstream compression, flow control, and LNG-adjacent equipment
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around midstream compression, flow-control, and LNG-adjacent equipment. The most relevant names are not commodity producers but asset owners and equipment/service platforms whose revenue is tied to gas gathering, processing, transportation, LNG, and installed-base maintenance. The underfollowed lane is strongest in contract compression providers such as Archrock and Kodiak Gas Services, where recurring service economics and fleet utilization can act as hidden signals for midstream demand. Chart Industries and Flowserve provide broader LNG/cryogenic and flow-control context, but they are more visible and less pure in different ways. Expanded the universe around midstream natural-gas compression, flow-control, and LNG-adjacent equipment. The reference lane is Baker Hughes because it anchors large-scale LNG compression, turbomachinery, and the pending Chart Industries acquisition. The underfollowed lane is more interesting for Serenity purposes: Archrock and Kodiak Gas Services provide direct contract-compression exposure with installed-base and service economics, while Matrix Service is a smaller, more speculative LNG-adjacent infrastructure contractor tied to cryogenic storage and terminal work. These are second-order picks-and-shovels names rather than commodity producers. Layer 1B expanded the node into a two-lane universe: one direct LNG equipment reference name and three underfollowed/niche industrial-service names tied to natural-gas compression, modular gas infrastructure, and flow-control equipment.
